transcript.text: Alright everyone, we're two weeks out from the first production customer launch of the event-ingestion service. Per our normal architecture-review routine, I need to hear the final checks from both application architecture and compliance before I record the operating plan and make the binding architecture decision. Both the streaming and hourly batch architectures passed the functional test suite in dev, so we're ready to move forward with the review. Who wants to start with the application architecture final check?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While testing an unrelated replay tool yesterday, I measured a launch-period burst of about 18,000 events per minute that the hourly batch design cannot process within the customer-facing latency target. The streaming design needs exactly 12 partitions for that load, and the launch plan must include provisioning those 12 partitions and validating replay capacity before launch. I have not yet updated the architecture document because the replay test was outside the launch checklist.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to raise a compliance requirement that I haven't yet added to the launch review. I confirmed with the privacy office this morning that the first customer's event payloads must remain in the EU and be retained for exactly 400 days for an audit requirement. The launch plan must include a data-residency control confirming that payloads remain in the EU. This was captured in a separate compliance system via the customer questionnaire, so it wasn't reflected in the launch review checklist yet.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Provision exactly 12 partitions for the streaming architecture to handle the launch-period burst of approximately 18,000 events per minute.
Validate replay capacity before launch as identified during the replay tool testing.
Implement and confirm a data-residency control ensuring all event payloads remain in the EU.
Configure event payload retention for exactly 400 days to meet the audit requirement.
